clue.text: Is the equator the answer for summit talks ?

definitions.text: Is the equator the answer for summit talks ?

parts.words: Is the equator the answer for summit talks ?
parts.note: the equator is the hot band round the earth, a ... on the map, and a direct phone link between world leaders carries their summit talks

explanation.surface: A geography question asking whether the equator could serve as a venue for summit talks.
explanation.walkthrough: The equator is the hottest line on the globe; the same two words name the direct phone link set up between Washington and Moscow for leaders to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct telephone link between heads of government lets them hold summit-level talks at once.

clue.text: Funny-sounding bone

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: funny means humorous

explanation.surface: The funny bone, named for how it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'funny bone' is the nerve at the elbow, at the end of this upper-arm bone; the clue says humorous and the bone's name sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The long bone of the upper arm, running from shoulder to elbow.

clue.text: Avert retribution for starting a fire

definitions.meaning: the superstitious phrase said, while tapping timber, to ward off bad luck after tempting fate
dry rotten wood used as tinder

explanation.surface: Advice on avoiding punishment for arson.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it wards off ill fortune; as a noun it is decayed wood that catches a spark, tinder.

clue.text: Opening in diamonds here in Asia

indicators.note: the answer is the opening stretch of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Diamond mines being opened up somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the first five letters of 'in diamonds'.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South Asian country, famous for its historic diamond mines such as Golconda.

clue.text: Outpourings of notes on mergers

parts.note: E and F are two notes of the musical scale
fusions are mergers

explanation.surface: Gushing memos written about company mergers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gushing expressions of feeling, or floods of liquid poured out.

clue.text: Masterpiece of a type to copy

definitions.text: Masterpiece of a type to copy

parts.words: Masterpiece of a type to copy
parts.note: read as 'master piece': in office duplicating, the cut waxed sheet that every copy is run off from is the master

explanation.surface: Praise for a work of art so fine it deserves to be imitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masterpiece' suggests great art, but split it: a duplicating machine prints from a master sheet, and the cut sheet used on a Gestetner-type copier is this.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut sheet through which ink is pressed acts as the master from which copies of a design are made.

clue.text: Many fish in shallow water

definitions.meaning: a large group of fish swimming together
a sandbank or shallow place in the sea

explanation.surface: A crowd of fish gathered in the shallows.
explanation.definitionFit: A school of fish; also a submerged sandbank making the sea shallow.

clue.text: Tired of spent petrol fumes ?

definitions.meaning: read as made of exhaust, the fumes a car engine gives off

explanation.surface: A motorist weary of breathing car fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out; and, read as 'exhaust-ed', made of the spent gases from an engine.

clue.text: Arboreal form of locust

parts.note: not the insect but the Mediterranean tree whose pods, locust beans, are eaten

explanation.surface: A naturalist describing a species of locust that lives in trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locust' suggests the insect, but the locust tree's pods are the chocolate substitute, so its tree form is this.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean tree whose edible pods are called locust beans or St John's bread.

clue.text: Increased plant's output radically

parts.note: radically means by roots: a gardener pegs a shoot to the soil so it roots and becomes a new plant

explanation.surface: A factory boss who sharply increased production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory and 'radically' drastic change; but radical means of the root, and gardeners multiply plants by rooting bent-down shoots in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Propagating by pegging stems into soil to root multiplies the plant through its roots.

clue.text: No mud used in making this earthwork

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are put to use in building something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder boasting that an earth bank was raised without any mud.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says no mud went in, yet the letters of NO MUD are exactly what is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised heap of earth, such as a barrow or rampart, is a basic earthwork.

clue.text: It's rash to cheat the novelist

parts.note: to fool someone is to trick or cheat them
Thomas Hardy, author of Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: A warning that it would be reckless to swindle a famous author.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless boldness without thought of danger is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Preparing for the Buckingham Show

parts.note: a practice run before a performance, and also the title of the 1671 satirical play by George Villiers, Duke of Buckingham

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a grand display at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buckingham' suggests the palace, but it is the Duke of Buckingham, whose famous burlesque play bears this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice performance is how a cast prepares for the real show, and the Duke's play has this name.

clue.text: River does not aspire to colour

indicators.note: aspirating a word means sounding its H, so a word that does not aspire drops its H

parts.note: the Humber is the estuary in north-east England

explanation.surface: A river that lacks ambition to become something vivid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspire' looks like ambition but means aspirate, sounding an H; drop the H of HUMBER, the estuary in Yorkshire, as a speaker who drops aitches would.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown earth pigment used by painters, so a brownish shade.

clue.text: Conqueror's air-attack ?

parts.note: A falcon's swoop down on its prey is also called by this word

explanation.surface: A question about how a conquering general would strike from the skies.
explanation.walkthrough: From the title of Goldsmith's play 'She Stoops to Conquer': the conqueror's move is the falconer's word for a hawk diving on prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's swift plunge from height onto its quarry is called by this term.

clue.text: Newspaper company demanding, ing compulsory service

parts.note: the press is newspapers
a gang is a company of people

explanation.surface: A newspaper firm insisting staff do national service.
explanation.walkthrough: A press gang seized men for compulsory service in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval party that forced men into service, so a group demanding conscripted service.

clue.text: Not in steady form, but beat the rest in the long run

definitions.text: beat the rest in the long run

parts.note: out is the opposite of in

indicators.note: the letters of the word steady are given a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: An athlete who ran unevenly yet still outlasted the field in a long race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' reshapes STEADY into STAYED, placed after OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain longer than others is to outlast them, winning by endurance.

clue.text: Who's been sleeping in my bed ? C. Robin might ask

definitions.text: Who's been sleeping in my bed ? C. Robin might ask

parts.words: Who's been sleeping in my bed ? C. Robin might ask
parts.note: the Goldilocks bears' question, asked by Christopher Robin about his own toy companion from the Pooh stories

explanation.surface: The Goldilocks question, put by Christopher Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: The three bears ask 'Who's been sleeping in my bed?'; Christopher Robin, in A. A. Milne's books, would find his stuffed bear Winnie-the-Pooh there.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffed toy animal children take to bed, like Christopher Robin's Pooh.

clue.text: Weapon of adolescent society?

parts.note: a cudgel belonging to the young, which also names a recreational society for teenagers

explanation.surface: A question about what arms a gang of teenagers carry.
explanation.walkthrough: A cudgel is a club, and a club for the young is a teenage recreation centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised social centre for teenagers, a club for the young.

clue.text: Slipped out of gear ? Alignment not checked

definitions.meaning: having taken off one's clothes, gear being clothing
to dress ranks is the drill term for aligning soldiers, so ranks not so aligned are without dressing

explanation.surface: A driver whose car jumped out of gear because the wheels were badly aligned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' suggests a car, but it is clothes; on parade, 'dress!' orders the ranks into a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked after shedding clothes; and, in military drill, ranks whose line has not been straightened.

clue.text: Honoured companion in utter confusion in Holland

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the jumbled letters
the letters of utter are thrown into confusion

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A decorated person utterly lost somewhere in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' scrambles UTTER into UTRET, and 'in' puts CH inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch city and province, so a place found in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Take action about our Spanish river

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, around, the second

parts.note: to do is to act

explanation.surface: A call to protect a beloved river in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river rising in Spain and flowing through Portugal to Porto.

clue.text: The old boy's remedy is not clear

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil, plus the 's
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: An elderly man's home remedy whose workings are mysterious.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard to understand or dim, the opposite of plain.

clue.text: Clothes Pierre is after for a terrorist

definitions.text: Clothes Pierre is after for a terrorist

parts.words: Clothes Pierre is after for a terrorist
parts.note: garments followed by the name Pierre spell out the surname of the Jacobin leader of the French Reign of Terror

explanation.surface: A Frenchman shopping for an outfit fit for a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means clothes; put PIERRE after it and you get ROBESPIERRE, architect of the Terror in revolutionary France.
explanation.definitionFit: Long loose gowns are garments, and joined to Pierre they name the French revolutionary.

clue.text: Disney creature — no extra to a little Italian boy

indicators.note: the word no is extra to the answer, so the Italian word less that word gives it

parts.note: bambino is Italian for a baby or little child
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Disney character who is not much bigger than a small Italian child.
explanation.walkthrough: Add NO to the answer and you have BAMBINO, Italian for a little child; so take NO away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fawn hero of Disney's 1942 animated film.

clue.text: Aurora made for the roof

definitions.meaning: the northern or southern lights shining in the heavens

explanation.surface: Dawn light designed especially to shine through the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora is lights in the heavens; roof windows let daylight in from above.

clue.text: Misses out principal bowlers

definitions.meaning: in the game of bowls, the captain of a rink is called this

explanation.surface: The leading bowlers left out of a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowlers' suggests cricket, but in lawn bowls the captain of each team is its skip.
explanation.definitionFit: Passes over, omitting; and in lawn bowls, team captains.

clue.text: One member is forming war-parties in Africa

parts.note: Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician joining an armed band in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Zulu regiments of warriors, bands assembled for war in southern Africa.

clue.text: Temporary shelter by a river, where college youths go for a change

definitions.text: where college youths go for a change

parts.note: a camp is a temporary place of shelter
the Nile in Africa

explanation.surface: Students on holiday pitching a tent by a river for a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'college youths' sounds like students, but the Ancient Society of College Youths is a London bell-ringing society, and a 'change' is a sequence in change-ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-standing bell tower is where bell-ringers go to ring changes.

clue.text: Savoury rice for the Italian in a French town

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Pau is a town in south-west France
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A rice dish served to an Italian visiting a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiced rice dish of the Middle East and India, also spelt pilaf.

clue.text: Flying member in a set-back, caused by sharp pains

indicators.note: the first piece takes the other inside it
the word set, as in 'set-back', is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a wing is the limb a bird flies with

explanation.surface: A bird hurt in a setback, suffering stabbing pains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' reads as a misfortune but tells you to reverse SET, giving TES, around WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden brief stabs of pain are pangs.

clue.text: Inclined to laugh when getting one pound returned in pay increase

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the pay increase

parts.note: a rise is a pay increase
the Roman numeral I is one
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A worker amused when a pay rise brings in a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LB into BL, so I and BL go inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense meaning given to laughter, besides the usual sense of laughable.
